## Reading Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data <- read_csv("w1-teacher-student-scored-aggregated.csv")
```

```{r}


# Remove non-relevant columns
data_clean <- data |> 
  select(-SID)

# Select only numeric columns
numeric_df <- data_clean |> 
  select(where(is.numeric))

# Loop through numeric columns and display density plots
for (col_name in colnames(numeric_df)) {
  p <- ggplot(numeric_df, aes_string(x = col_name)) +
    geom_density(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6) +
    labs(title = paste("Density Plot of", col_name),
         x = col_name,
         y = "Density") +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p)
}
```

### Shapiro Test

```{r}
shapiro_results <- map_dfr(names(numeric_df), function(var) {
  values <- numeric_df[[var]]
  if (length(unique(values)) < 3) {
    tibble(Variable = var, W = NA, p_value = NA, Note = "Too few unique values")
  } else {
    test <- shapiro.test(values)
    tibble(Variable = var, W = round(test$statistic, 10), p_value = round(test$p.value, 10), Note = NA)
  }
})

shapiro_results

```

```{r}
data_clean |> 
  psych::describe()
```

```{r}
library(reshape2)
cor_matrix <- cor(data_clean, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

# Melt into long format
cor_melted <- melt(cor_matrix)

# Plot heatmap
ggplot(cor_melted, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white",
    midpoint = 0, limit = c(-1, 1), space = "Lab",
    name = "Correlation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Correlation Heatmap",
    x = "", y = ""
  )
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Compute correlation matrix
cor_mat <- cor(data_clean)

# Step 2: Convert to long format
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

cor_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor_mat)) %>%
  rename(Var1 = Var1, Var2 = Var2, Correlation = Freq)

# Step 3: Filter pairs with |correlation| > 0.6, and remove self-correlations and duplicates
strong_corrs <- cor_long %>%
  filter(abs(Correlation) > 0.6, Var1 != Var2) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pair = paste(sort(c(Var1, Var2)), collapse = "_")) %>%
  distinct(pair, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(-pair)

print(strong_corrs)
write_csv(strong_corrs, "strong_corrs.csv")

```
